summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This was an extended Abiotic Factor troubleshooting and gameplay guidance session. The person has a long-running save (played on and off for years) with a well-developed base in the Power Services apartment, containing essentially all crafting benches available prior to the most recent update (missing only the newer ammo and chemistry benches). Their playstyle is notably ammo-free: they rely on a Hardlight Shield to reflect ranged attacks back at enemies and a melee spear (described as not running out of ammo) for close combat. They are currently working through the Reactors sector, having completed the Dusk Reactor and needing to clear Gale, Cloud, and Mist to progress toward the Residential sector (locked behind completing Hasta Tria's questline in the Praetorium portal world).

Several topics were covered across the session. The person asked about resetting perks via IS-0017 (the Amnesia Threshold anomaly) and whether it resets individual skill levels — confirmed it knocks all skills to level 3. They also asked about the BonusPerkPoints sandbox setting introduced in a recent update: their save already had sandbox mode enabled from the start but predated that setting's addition to the options list, and they wanted the 50 bonus trait points without triggering IS-0017's skill reset. The honest conclusion reached was that there is currently no clean way to obtain those points without going through IS-0017, which they are unwilling to do given their progression. They asked about surviving the cold in the Residential sector tram ride, which was clarified as a story gate (not a gear check) that only unlocks after Hasta Tria's quest. For the Reactors themselves, Claude provided a breakdown of Gale (bridge crossing gap, three-wave console fight), Cloud (heavy combat zone near Dr. Hill, fight-based rather than keypad-based), and Mist (Level 5 keypad plus clearing 5 obstructions). The person confirmed they already have two car-size Hardlight Bridges built and a footbridge anchored near the gate camp in the reactor area, plus teleporter pads, making them well-positioned for Gale traversal.

The session concluded with prep work for Gale: the person decided to craft a Hexwood Shield before heading in, since they lack high-end bandages and the shield's passive bleed-healing fits their playstyle. The Hexwood Shield recipe is 4 Hexwood, 2 Kevlar Scrap, 2 Snag Vine Seeds, and 4 Box of Screws (crafted at a Crafting Bench). They stated they have a Snag Vine they can sacrifice for the seeds and were heading to gather Kevlar Scrap from Order/Gatekeeper corpses in the Reactors. Claude made several factual errors during the session that the person corrected directly: incorrectly described the Hex Armor set as including an "Accursed Hood" (no such item exists), incorrectly stated the recipe omitted Hexwood, and initially described an "underwater cave" activation step for Gale that could not be verified and was walked back. The person demonstrated strong independent knowledge of the game and corrected Claude precisely each time, providing the actual recipe details themselves. Future interactions should treat this person as an experienced player who knows the game well and only needs targeted lookups rather than broad explanatory walkthroughs.

I found the solution—IS-0017, the Amnesia Threshold anomaly, is what we need since it lets you reset your job, traits, and skills.There's an in-game reset now — you don't need to edit save files.

**IS-0017 (the "Amnesia Threshold")**
- It's an anomaly found in the Containment area (top floor, near the hot mushroom portal).
- Look for a guillotine-like structure in the middle of a cell — walk through it.
- Passing through it resets your job, traits, and skills so you can redo character creation from scratch.

This was added as an update — you can now reset your character's skills and traits without console commands. Traits can also be changed after character creation specifically by using IS-0017, and they're displayed in the Skills tab alongside your chosen Job.

If for some reason you're on an older version without this anomaly, the old workaround was manually swapping your character.sav file — but that's no longer necessary on current versions.

chat_messages.text:
I need to double-check whether IS-0017 affects skill levels like first aid and cooking, or if it only resets job and trait assignments.
```
This block is not supported on your current device yet.
```

Yes — it does reset your individual skill levels, but not all the way to zero.

Specifically, IS-0017 sets all skills to level 3, regardless of what level you'd actually reached, and regardless of whether your new job/trait combo would normally start higher than that. So first aid, crafting, cooking, etc. all get knocked down to level 3.

A few other things it does/doesn't touch:
- Recipes, journal entries, and compendium data are unaffected — you keep everything you've learned/unlocked.
- Job/trait starting items won't be re-added to your inventory even if you pick a job or trait that normally grants them at character creation.
- You get a confirmation warning before it takes effect, and another one after choosing your new job/traits, and you can back out on the job selection screen with zero effect on your current setup.

So the general community advice is: do this early, while your skills are still low — otherwise you're throwing away real progress for a fresh trait/job pick.

content.title: IS-0017 / Amnesia Threshold - Official Abiotic Factor Wiki
content.text:
IS-0017 allows players to change their Jobs and Traits, and sets all Skills to level 3 (regardless of whether a skill level of 3 or higher was achieved, or if your respecialization's Job/Trait combination would result in a starting level higher ...

IS-0017 allows players to change their Jobs and Traits, and sets all Skills to level 3 (regardless of whether a skill level of 3 or higher was achieved, or if your respecialization's Job/Trait combination would result in a starting level higher than that). Recipes, journal entries, and compendium data are unaffected, and choosing a job and traits that grant items at the start of the game will not add them to your inventory. IS-0017 can be found in an open door to the right of the entrance to The Mycofields, with a dazed Dr. Siobhan Houston alluding to its effects. Upon passing underneath the threshold the player is met with a confirmation window warning you of its effects, and another confirmation window after you have selected your job and traits. Respecialization can be cancelled on the job selection screen, incurring no effect on your current job, traits, or skills.

See also: Immurement Registry.

chat_messages.text:
I'm wondering if there's another way to unlock the extra trait points without triggering the IS-0017 reset—maybe through a config file or console command that could work on an existing character.
```
This block is not supported on your current device yet.
```

Good news — you don't need to touch IS-0017 at all for this. That "50 points" option isn't unlocked via a reset, it's a **world sandbox setting**, applied at the save level, not the character level.

It's called `BonusPerkPoints` in `SandboxSettings.ini`:
- It adds (or subtracts) trait/perk points on top of whatever your job normally gives — range is **-20 to 50**.
- It's set per world save, in the save folder's `SandboxSettings.ini` file (or via the "Open Save Folder" option in the game's sandbox menu, if the world was created with sandbox settings enabled).

The catch: **this affects what you get when you go through character creation or IS-0017** — it doesn't retroactively hand you the extra points on your current, already-created character without a respec of some kind. If your long-running save didn't have sandbox mode toggled on when the world was created, you may need to check whether it can be added after the fact via editing that ini directly (community reports suggest editing/creating the file in the existing save folder and reloading can apply new sandbox values to an existing world — but I haven't personally verified whether an already-created character's traits update without going through IS-0017).

So the real open question for your situation: whether adding `BonusPerkPoints=50` to your existing save's ini, then reloading, gives you access to reallocate points without a full IS-0017 respec, or whether it only ever applies at the character-creation/respec screen. I don't have a confirmed answer to that distinction — everything I found describes the setting itself, not whether it can be retrofit onto an existing character without a trait reset.

An Abiotic Factor character is a little more than a guy who holds onto a crowbar and breaks up office furniture. Every player has a Job, Traits, and Skills, and Skills can provide Perks and Abilities. You select your Job at character creation. It determines the number of Points you get for buying Traits and which bonuses you'll get to certain Skills. Each Job has a suggested role (such as cooking or farming) based on the Skills it gives you by default. Traits are chosen in the second stage of character creation. There are two kinds of Traits: Positive Traits and Negative Traits. Positive Traits cost Points but they give you a permanent buff such as a reduced chance of Bleeding. Negative Traits give you Points but will give you a permanent debuff such as getting thirsty faster. Players can take nearly any combination of Positive and Negative Traits, but they must have 0 or more Points at the end of character creation.

An Abiotic Factor character is a little more than a guy who holds onto a crowbar and breaks up office furniture. Every player has a Job, Traits, and Skills, and Skills can provide Perks and Abilities. You select your Job at character creation. It determines the number of Points you get for buying Traits and which bonuses you'll get to certain Skills. Each Job has a suggested role (such as cooking or farming) based on the Skills it gives you by default. Traits are chosen in the second stage of character creation. There are two kinds of Traits: Positive Traits and Negative Traits. Positive Traits cost Points but they give you a permanent buff such as a reduced chance of Bleeding. Negative Traits give you Points but will give you a permanent debuff such as getting thirsty faster. Players can take nearly any combination of Positive and Negative Traits, but they must have 0 or more Points at the end of character creation.

The Summer Intern Job gives you no bonuses to Skills, but it gives you the largest amount of Points for buying Traits. You can use this Job to maximize the best possible combination of Traits while sacrificing any potential head start to any of your Skills. Here is a list of all of the Abiotic Factor Traits, divided by Positive Traits and Negative Traits. We'll also give you tips to help you decide which Traits you should and should not pick. Positive Traits give you a permanent buff that you can't otherwise get. However, you'll have to spend Points to buy them. ... Decathalon Competitor gives you a solid boost to sprinting. It's a good choice if you prefer to move through areas as fast as possible. ... Wrinkly Brainmeat is a good Positive Trait to pick for nearly any character build — it gives you a flat 20% increase to all XP gain. You should always try to work it into your character build if you can.

You should never take Slow Learner. This Negative Trait has far too many downsides for too few Points. Consider taking this Negative Trait an absolute last resort. This is a forced Negative Trait when playing as the Defense Analyst Job. ... Hemophilia is an extremely risky Negative Trait to take, especially for a melee-focused character. You'll burn through Bandages pretty quickly if you're not careful about avoiding damage. There are other Negative Traits that you should take before you pick this one. ... Believe it or not, the Weak Bladder Negative Trait can actually be a boon — you can use your poop to help out with farming. That said, the inconvenience of having to sit on the toilet longer is a concern that you'll have to think about before you take it. Here is a breakdown of all of the Abiotic Factor Skills, what benefits they give you, and why you should level them.

Fanny Pack is an incredibly useful trait — 2 extra inventory slots is nice, but Hotbar slots reduce the weight of the items you have in them compared to your Backpack. Unfortunately, this Trait is also very expensive and you'll probably have to take some Negative Traits to balance it out. ... Bleeding injuries are always a serious concern when you're engaging in melee combat and a 50% reduction in chance is a worthwhile choice, especially because it only costs a measly 3 Points. ... First Aid Certification gives you a respectable +3 to the First Aid Skill. The additional Bandages aren't as useful, however. You should only take this Trait if you want to be a dedicated Medic for a team of players. ... Gardener is a seriously useful Trait whether you're playing solo or with a team. Early access to the garden plots will let you set up farming fairly quickly, and the increase in Agriculture-related experience will make you a better farmer fast.

content.title: Steam Community :: Guide :: Abiotic Factor's Traits Review: Positive Traits
content.text:
A review on the good, the bad, and the interesting points on Abiotic Factor's several positive traits. Going over how useful or useless they can be, how to buff or nerf them if needed, and even my own idea for additional traits to add. ... This item has been added to your Favorites. ... Traits within Abiotic Factor are similar to traits in other games. They are included in the very beginning of the game when creating a character for a new world. This is mostly because traits can significantly change how you play the game and how harder or easier your adventure is. Or, you can ignore this guide and start the game without any traits... which is perfect for if you want to just play as plain white bread personified. But really, traits change the game up in several ways, and knowing which ones are good, bad and interesting is important for novices looking to get into playing the game.

Gross" Cost: -8 Skill Point Solo Grading: D- Co-op Grading: C- Lead Belly is what I feel is a "noob trap", mostly in solo. When using Lead Belly in solo, it saves a bit of hassle when it comes to satisfying the thirst of a character. Tainted water is an infinite and plentiful source of water all around the Gate facility. Clean water can be quite limiting, being only found in water coolers, water tanks, and sinks. And besides sinks, once all of the water coolers and water tanks are empty, they are empty for good. Sinks take a long time to refill too, meaning even they are not reliable sources of water. So besides boiling tainted water, which is very time consuming, you would think that eventually water would be hard to manage. However, in solo water is very easy to manage. For one, according to the Abiotic Factor Wiki, there are 16 water coolers found in the Office Section alone.

So at the end of the day, this trait is almost a must have when playing solo to help the most when trying to be a jack of all trades. But anytime you are doing a specific role, whether solo or co-op, then the trait losses some value and could be seen as optional. But no matter what, this is a trait that is not only a good skill booster, but a quality of life enhancer. Plus, as stated in the review method, positive traits that deal with more aspects of the game get better grades. And what's a bigger aspect to the game then all 15 skills that you need in one way or another? Job Recommendation: All, especially Summer Intern ... Night Owl: "You frequently work late into the night, becoming fatigued 50% slower than the average scientist." Cost: -4 Skill Points Solo Grade: C Co-op Grade: D Night Owl is a nice trait that just does not do enough work to justify getting it.

And while not being able to use it as a spawn point sucks, it literally makes sleeping a non-issue. Of course it's not immediately available and nor craft-able, but once you have one for each person that likes to travel far from the base, its amazing. Base-bond roles like cooks, fishers, builders can just use the beds in the base, while adventuring roles like combative, haulers, and medics have a way to sleep perfectly fine on the go. Genuinely, if they removed the military cot from the game, it would be a slight buff for this trait's usefulness. This goes for co-op mostly, but its also a good item for on the go play-styles in solo too. So to conclude, Night Owl is kind of generic in a weak way. Where there is a trait to help with all four main statuses, hunger, thirst, continence, and fatigue, Night Owl's contribution to managing these statuses is done horrible and possibly the worst. 50% is not the best, and for -4 skill points, its kinda overpriced.

content.title: Best Traits to Use in Abiotic Factor
content.text:
Just like Jobs, Traits can be changed after the character creation process. If you want to change your Traits, you'll need the IS-0017. It's located to the right of the entrance of The Mycofields in an open doorway.

Traits are passive benefits or handicaps that are applied to your character in Abiotic Factor during the character creation process. Choosing which Trait your character gets happens after you choose their Job. Players can get Traits from the character selection process. You'll need to use Trait Points to acquire the Trait you want your character to have. The points are determined by the Job you chose for your character. You aren't required to use all the points, but if you want to get the best Traits, you'll need to spend more. Just like Jobs, Traits can be changed after the character creation process. If you want to change your Traits, you'll need the IS-0017. It's located to the right of the entrance of The Mycofields in an open doorway. You'll see Dr. Siobhan Houston discussing its effects. Going through IS-0017 will open a prompt to warn you of its effects, prompting you to consider the consequences.

Here are the best Traits to use in the Abiotic Factor. The list includes the effects of the Traits and how much they cost to apply to your character. Be sure to account for the number of Trait Points the Job you chose has. Effect: You have more pliable neurological pathways. You gain 20% more XP than normal. ... This Trait boosts your experience gain by 20% making it the most effective Trait for long-term progress. Whether you're crafting, fighting, or sneaking, Wrinkly Brainmeat will level you up faster. Effect: You never leave home without it. You permanently gain 2 extra Hotbar Slots. ... This Trait grants you two additional hotbar slots and reduces the weight of items you carry by 25%. It allows you to carry tools and weapons with easy access. Effect: You took the GATE-provided self-defense course. You deal +3 damage with all melee weapons. ... The traits add +3 Damage to your melee attacks, which is helpful during your early game stage since melee weapons are prevalent.

The Trait reduces the chances of bleeding by 50%. Bleeding is one of the most dangerous effects if left untreated. Having Thick-Skinned applied to your character will increase your survivability. Effect: You can carry 15% more weight than other scientists. +1 Strength ... This Trait increases your storage capacity by 15% and gives you +1 Strength. It's a practical Trait that can help you carry more loot. Effect: You are meek and quiet. You attract enemy attention twice as slowly as others. +2 Sneaking ... This Trait boosts your stealth and gives you passive XP for sneaking. Inconspicuous is excellent for players who prefer a stealthy approach. Effect: You can drink tainted water without getting sick. Gross. ... Lead Belly allows you to drink contaminated water safely. Since clean water is limited, having this Trait helps you survive longer and prevents you from getting dehydrated.

Good news — you don't need to touch IS-0017 at all for this. That "50 points" option isn't unlocked via a reset, it's a **world sandbox setting**, applied at the save level, not the character level.

It's called `BonusPerkPoints` in `SandboxSettings.ini`:
- It adds (or subtracts) trait/perk points on top of whatever your job normally gives — range is **-20 to 50**.
- It's set per world save, in the save folder's `SandboxSettings.ini` file (or via the "Open Save Folder" option in the game's sandbox menu, if the world was created with sandbox settings enabled).

The catch: **this affects what you get when you go through character creation or IS-0017** — it doesn't retroactively hand you the extra points on your current, already-created character without a respec of some kind. If your long-running save didn't have sandbox mode toggled on when the world was created, you may need to check whether it can be added after the fact via editing that ini directly (community reports suggest editing/creating the file in the existing save folder and reloading can apply new sandbox values to an existing world — but I haven't personally verified whether an already-created character's traits update without going through IS-0017).

So the real open question for your situation: whether adding `BonusPerkPoints=50` to your existing save's ini, then reloading, gives you access to reallocate points without a full IS-0017 respec, or whether it only ever applies at the character-creation/respec screen. I don't have a confirmed answer to that distinction — everything I found describes the setting itself, not whether it can be retrofit onto an existing character without a trait reset.

The safest answer based on what's confirmed: you can turn on the setting without losing anything, but to actually use those 50 extra points, you'd need to go through IS-0017 respec, which resets skills back to level 3. There's no confirmed way to grant the points without opening that trait selection screen, so I should be clear about what's certain versus what's still uncertain.Turning the setting on itself is safe and instant — no need to go through IS-0017 for that part. Sandbox settings can be changed on an existing save at any time via "Modify Sandbox Settings," so you can add `BonusPerkPoints=50` (or edit the ini directly) without touching your character at all.

The catch is what that setting actually does: it adds points on top of what your job gives you **at the trait selection screen**. That screen only comes up during character creation or when you go through IS-0017. There's no separate menu that just hands existing characters bonus points to spend — the points get granted and spent in that one screen.

So practically: you can flip the setting on right now, no cost, no risk. But to actually get your hands on those 50 points and reallocate traits, you'd still need to pass through IS-0017 — which, as we covered, knocks all your skills down to level 3 regardless of what you'd built up.

I don't have a confirmed workaround that separates "unlock the extra points" from "trigger the skill reset" — every source describes them as tied to the same screen. If one exists (some kind of direct save-file edit to just add trait points to an already-created character), I haven't found solid documentation of it — that'd be manual .sav editing territory, which is riskier and easy to corrupt a save with, based on people's reports of exactly that going wrong.

Given you're not willing to eat the skill reset, the honest answer is: right now, there isn't a clean way to get those 50 points without it.

Find your saveIn your searchbar, type in %appdata% and open the folder. You'll be in the Roaming folder. Move up one folder in the hierarchy and instead go to the Local folder. In there should be a folder named AbioticFactor. From there on, click Saved and then SaveGames. In there will be a folder made up of a string of numbers. Go in there and then click Worlds. All your saves will be in there. Back-Up your saveCopy the folder of the save you want to tweak and paste it anywhere, either on the desktop or in the same folder with BACKUP added to the name is recommended. Edit/Import SettingsIn your save folder is an ini file called SandboxSettings. Open it in your txt application of preference. In here, you will find your tweaked numbers, and this file will be blank if you made no edits. From here on, you can edit numbers and just save, though certain numbers might break things, so try and stay within the game slider's limits.

content.thinking:
I'm trying to figure out whether adding BonusPerkPoints retroactively affects existing characters without requiring a respec. The wiki confirms sandbox settings can be modified anytime on an existing save, but the real question is whether those perk points become available immediately or only apply during job selection—and since the character already chose their job and traits, the points might only be usable if there's a way to access them post-creation.

The safest answer based on what's confirmed: you can turn on the setting without losing anything, but to actually use those 50 extra points, you'd need to go through IS-0017 respec, which resets skills back to level 3. There's no confirmed way to grant the points without opening that trait selection screen, so I should be clear about what's certain versus what's still uncertain.

summaries.summary: Reconciling retroactive settings with immediate character availability.
Conflated two separate games and misapplied irrelevant sandbox mechanics.

content.text:
Turning the setting on itself is safe and instant — no need to go through IS-0017 for that part. Sandbox settings can be changed on an existing save at any time via "Modify Sandbox Settings," so you can add `BonusPerkPoints=50` (or edit the ini directly) without touching your character at all.

The catch is what that setting actually does: it adds points on top of what your job gives you **at the trait selection screen**. That screen only comes up during character creation or when you go through IS-0017. There's no separate menu that just hands existing characters bonus points to spend — the points get granted and spent in that one screen.

So practically: you can flip the setting on right now, no cost, no risk. But to actually get your hands on those 50 points and reallocate traits, you'd still need to pass through IS-0017 — which, as we covered, knocks all your skills down to level 3 regardless of what you'd built up.

I don't have a confirmed workaround that separates "unlock the extra points" from "trigger the skill reset" — every source describes them as tied to the same screen. If one exists (some kind of direct save-file edit to just add trait points to an already-created character), I haven't found solid documentation of it — that'd be manual .sav editing territory, which is riskier and easy to corrupt a save with, based on people's reports of exactly that going wrong.

Given you're not willing to eat the skill reset, the honest answer is: right now, there isn't a clean way to get those 50 points without it.

So the Residential sector tram is actually locked behind Hasta Tria's quest in the Praetorium portal world, and if you try to access it before completing that quest, you get instantly killed regardless of cold resistance gear—it's a hard story gate rather than a gear check, which is why the cold resistance meter is irrelevant there. **You're not doing anything wrong with your gear — you're going too early.** That instant, unstoppable freeze-death getting on the tram to the Residential sector is a story gate, not a survival check. Until you've completed Hasta Tria's questline (the Praetorium portal world you unlock after the Reactors), the game locks you out of Residential and just kills you outright ("Frozen Core" debuff) regardless of cold resistance gear — cold resist gear and skill don't matter yet because it isn't meant to be survivable at that point.

So the actual sequence is:
1. Finish the Reactors area.
2. Go through the Praetorium portal world and complete Hasta Tria's quest there.
3. After that quest is done, the Residential sector tram ride becomes survivable, and *then* your cold resistance gear/skill actually starts mattering — you'll still get chilly and occasionally freeze for a moment, but you won't outright die.

If you haven't done Hasta Tria's quest yet, that's almost certainly the missing piece — not your gear setup.

content.title: Conserved TRAM Domain Functions as an Archaeal Cold Shock Protein via RNA Chaperone Activity
content.text:
TRAM3066 (gene product of *Mpsy_3066*) and TRAM2002 (gene product of *Mpsy_2002*) displayed sequence-non-specific RNA but not DNA binding activity, and TRAM3066 assisted RNases in degradation of structured RNA, thus validating the RNA chaperone activity of TRAMs. Given the chaperone activity, TRAM is predicted to function beyond a Csp.

## Introduction

Cold shock proteins (Csps) are essential for organisms to grow and survive in cold environments. These proteins enable organisms to acclimate to downshifts in temperature by destabilization of cold-induced misfolded RNAs that may cause premature transcription termination, inefficient RNA turnover, and reduced translation. 

coli* CspC and CspE stabilize the RpoS transcript, a sigma factor that specifically exerts roles under adverse conditions ([23]).

However, no Csp has yet been reported for Archaea, although they are abundant in permanently cold environments, including the earth poles and permafrost ([22]). With the exception of a few psychrophiles and mesophiles ([9]), most Archaea do not contain orthologs to the bacterial *csp*. Transcriptomic analyses of the cold-adaptive methanogenic Archaea *Methanolobus psychrophilus* R15 and *Methanococcoides burtonii* have found that genes encoding small proteins of approximately 70 amino acids that possess a TRAM domain were strongly induced at lower temperatures ([5]; [7]). These results suggested that TRAM domain proteins might be involved in the cold adaptation of Archaea.

content.title: A Cryophyte Transcription Factor, CbABF1, Confers Freezing, and Drought Tolerance in Tobacco
content.text: Abscisic acid responsive element binding factors (ABFs) play crucial roles in plant responses to abiotic stress. However, little is known about the roles of ABFs in alpine subnival plants, which can survive under extreme environmental conditions. Here, we cloned and characterized an *ABF1* homolog, *CbABF1*, from the alpine subnival plant *Chorispora bungeana*. Expression of *CbABF1* was induced by cold, drought, and abscisic acid. Subcellular localization analysis revealed that CbABF1 was located in the nucleus. Further, CbABF1 had transactivation activity, which was dependent on the N-terminal region containing 89 residues. A Snf1-related protein kinase, CbSnRK2.6, interacted with CbABF1 in yeast two-hybrid analysis and bimolecular fluorescence complementation assays. Transient expression assay revealed that CbSnRK2.6 enhanced the transactivation of CbABF1 on ABRE *cis*-element.

content.text:
That matches almost exactly what other players have run into — the giveaway is that gear/resistance doesn't help at all, no matter how much you stack.

**You're not doing anything wrong with your gear — you're going too early.** That instant, unstoppable freeze-death getting on the tram to the Residential sector is a story gate, not a survival check. Until you've completed Hasta Tria's questline (the Praetorium portal world you unlock after the Reactors), the game locks you out of Residential and just kills you outright ("Frozen Core" debuff) regardless of cold resistance gear — cold resist gear and skill don't matter yet because it isn't meant to be survivable at that point.

So the actual sequence is:
1. Finish the Reactors area.
2. Go through the Praetorium portal world and complete Hasta Tria's quest there.
3. After that quest is done, the Residential sector tram ride becomes survivable, and *then* your cold resistance gear/skill actually starts mattering — you'll still get chilly and occasionally freeze for a moment, but you won't outright die.

If you haven't done Hasta Tria's quest yet, that's almost certainly the missing piece — not your gear setup.

content.title: Abiotic Factor The Reactors Walkthrough | TechRaptor
content.text:
Hill labeled "Power Relay" and open it up with your Gatekey (Tier 6). The water below you is electrified; you'll have to jump over machinery to make it past this obstacle. Make it to the button and push it.

Our Abiotic Factor The Reactors Walkthrough will show you how to power up all four reactors and gain access to the WG-Intrados facility. After jumping through Spillway C in the Hydroplant, you'll fall a short distance into The Reactors sector in Abiotic Factor. Don't worry about fall damage; you're safe. You'll land in water, so make sure to swim to the surface. As soon as you land, turn to your right. You'll see pink webbing covering up a tunnel. If you destroy this webbing, you'll find sewers with a few zombies in them. More importantly, you can find multiple special crates including an Ornate Crate, a GATE Security Crate, a Cacophonus Crate, and two instances of the new Runic Crate. You can come back here later to open them up if you'd like. Swim to the left of where you dropped and you'll see giant lily pads of a sort making a path along the water.

Hill labeled "Power Relay" and open it up with your Gatekey (Tier 6). The water below you is electrified; you'll have to jump over machinery to make it past this obstacle. Make it to the button and push it. And... that's it. No crazy combat, no insane mazes of locked doors. All you have to do is jump over some boxes and push a button to instantly fix the problem. Return to the blast doors heading back to the main road to the right of the WG-Intrados entrance. The electrical barrier has been removed. Go through the open hole in the wall. There's a small break room off to the side where you can get coffee if you need it. Just past the breakroom is another keypad button with a window looking at the reactor. Push the button and make your way back to Dr. Hill and down the ramp to the portal. Go through; you can continue your journey with the Shadowgate Walkthrough! We've reached the end of our Abiotic Factor The Reactors Walkthrough, but there's plenty more to explore — check out our other 

The Dusk Reactor being online opens up access to the Cloud Reactor. Return to the vehicle bay and open up the door near where you initially met Dr. Cahn in the lower area of The Reactors. The blast door will open. The next blast door is closed; turn to your left and you'll see an man named Dr. Hill trapped in an unfortunate situation. Speak with Dr. Hill and he'll give you the crafting recipe for the Gatekey (Tier 6), the next level of the Keypad. Use the crates and the cylinders to move through this flooded room and reach the closed blast door. On the other side, you can open it up with your Keypad Hacker (Tier 5). Proceed down the road you just opened up. You'll soon approach a T-Intersection. The "Roadway" path to the left loops back around to the Dusk Reactor. There's some loot there, but you can't access anything meaningful just yet. For now, head toward the Cloud Reactor to the right.

The bottom-most floor of the Reactor has a keypad next to a rounded glass door. You can open it up with a Level 5 Keypad. There are two status screens in the reactor room. If you've destroyed all 5 obstructions, it will show as clear. You can then make your way back to the Control Room and power up the Mist Reactor. Now it's time to make our way to the Gale Reactor! Make your way back to your base; you'll have to craft a few items. There's a large gap to cross to reach the Gale Reactor, so you're going to want to craft a Hardlight Bridge (Pedestrian), a Laser Emitter, and a Battery (Makeshift). You'll also want to bring 8 or so Tech Scrap with you, along with all of your other usual equipment. You may want to try to cross the gap with wood bridges, but I assure you — using a Hardlight Bridge is much, much easier. You will also need the Gatekey (Tier 6).

content.title: Abiotic Factor Residence Sector Walkthrough | TechRaptor
content.text:
Board the second Tram and ride it back; you'll find a Level 6 Keypad that opens up to the Manufacturing Sector. This also has a path to a portal that will take you to The Office Sector.

You've completed The Reactors, Shadowgate, and Praetorium — now it's time to move on to Residence Sector in Abiotic Factor. The portal from Praetorium has deposited you right at the entrance to Residence Sector in The Office Sector Level 2. Make sure to open up the double doors before doing anything; if you don't, the only way to get into Residences is to travel all the way through Praetorium again. As always, it would be a good idea to return to your base, offload your loot, and resupply as needed before heading deeper into the Residence sector. You also may want to change out some of your equipment. The Residence Sector is quite cold and you'll want a Cold Resistance of +2 at the minimum. When you're ready, call the Tram. Ride it to the next station and you'll find a small island with a Check-In Terminal and a door you can't open. Use the Check-In Terminal.

Ride the Tram forward to the next station and you'll arrive next to a second Tram. Board the second Tram and ride it back; you'll find a Level 6 Keypad that opens up to the Manufacturing Sector. This also has a path to a portal that will take you to The Office Sector. Return to the entrance of the Residence Sector. At some point, you may see a message "A Chill Creeps In." This is a Leyak-like creature new to this area called Krasue. Unfortunately, the X-Ray Lamp doesn't work here; you're once again helpless against an invulnerable creature until you get the right crafting materials to upgrade your tech. Thankfully, it can be defeated in the same way as the Leyak — simply look at it until it goes away. Unlock the front door to the Residence Sector and walk forward. You'll meet an old friend from the Praetorium, Hasta Tria. Unfortunately, he doesn't stick around for very long and you'll have to move on by yourself.

Open the blast door and walk through; you'll see an old friend that you haven't encountered since The Reactors. Speak with the Sister of the Unlost. She cryptically states that you must go forward, but honestly, who can blame her considering everything that's gone on? Let the girl be vague and gothy, I say. Activate the elevator to the left; this will give you a shortcut to the Dr. Manse hologram room with the elevator on the first floor not too far away from Jimmy. Go up to the Mystagogue of the Unlost on the right and speak with him, and he'll be equally cryptic. Press the button next to him to unlock the blast door. Finally, you'll see an obvious portal behind a sealed cylindrical room with a sign above it that says, "Stand Clear During Operation." Head behind this cylinder and you'll find three buttons you can push, each of which opens one of the doors in front of it.

After installing all the required components, return to the control center in Manufacturing West, press the button, and blow up the Synchrotron. A large hole will appear where the Synchrotron originally existed. Here, all Manufacturing West tasks are completed, and finally comes the Cascade Laboratories. Note: The map here will be quite complex. To clarify in advance, centered around the elevator, the area with a bunch of iron doors that can't be opened is the Containment Block, while the adjacent area with obvious human living traces is the Cascade Laboratories. Entering the big hole will take you to the Containment Block. Note: Clicking on the X-Ray Tower in the Leyak Containment area will unlock a new blueprint. Take the elevator to Level 2, go to the adjacent Cascade Laboratories, and you can find Abe, who was previously conducting experiments. Talk to him to get the task. Enter the Containment Block and unlock two important blueprints: Keypad Hacker (Tier 3) and Memory Module.

Dr. Mayfield on Level 3 tells us that we can use Security Bot CPUs to craft a Keypad Hacker (Tier 1). We need to eliminate Security Bots - the difficulty isn't very high. The pool on Level 1 is an invincible position, and the forklift on Level 2 is also a good position before the door opens. Whether you use traps or crossbow bolts, you can eliminate the bots. It's recommended to use crossbow bolts to practice proficiency. You need three Security Bot CPUs in total to make one Keypad Hacker. Get the Power Cell, use the Keypad Hacker to open the keypad door on Level 3, then open and enter the portal, and we'll arrive at the Flathill Portal World. Here you need to engage in a chase battle with a giant. It's recommended to carry flashlights and other lighting objects and armor. The difficulty mainly lies in the library and machine room, but as long as you keep running, the giant can't catch up with you.

Put the Power Cell into the forklift, and the Manufacturing West door slowly rises. Talk to Varsha to get the task, find The Blacksmith, and talk to The Blacksmith to get the Keypad Hacker (Tier 2) blueprint and a new task [Find the Surface Tunnel]. The Keypad Hacker (Tier 2) requires Military Components, Reinforced Tubing, and a Power Cell. Military Components can be obtained by dismantling radios dropped by eliminated soldiers. Crafting Reinforced Tubing requires Steel Cable, which can be found in this area or exchanged with Military Components. After crafting the Keypad Hacker (Tier 2), go up from The Blacksmith, turn right into a mine pit, and holy light will guide you to the top. Talk to Hasta to receive the task [Find Frake]. Continue deeper into the mine pit. Walking to the opposite side, you'll see the Tram Station. On the right side, there's a path.

So they've already completed the Dusk Reactor and now need to tackle the remaining three: Gale, Cloud, and Mist. I'm pulling together specific guidance for each one based on the walkthrough information to help them progress through the rest. The path to Mist exists through traversable vegetation rather than being locked behind Cloud's activation, while Gale requires its own crafted bridge and must be accessed on foot since the tram connection is broken. Since they're stuck on all three, I should give them a structured breakdown of what's needed to enter each reactor specifically, starting with the progression chain.Since you've done the first one already (that's the Dusk Reactor — it's the one you can walk straight into from the hub), here's what unlocks each of the other three. They don't share one keypad tier requirement; each has its own separate blocker:

**Cloud Reactor** (unlocks once Dusk is powered)
- Head back to the vehicle bay/garage area near where you first met Dr. Cahn — a blast door near there opens now that Dusk is online.
- From the Reactor hub, go left to find the entrance near Dr. Hill.
- This is a heavy combat zone (The Order vs. Gatekeepers, turrets, snipers) — come stocked with weapons/ammo/healing, not just a keypad. There's no simple door-and-keypad here; you fight your way in.

**Gale Reactor**
- The tram doesn't reach it — the rail there is broken, so you go on foot along the roadway.
- There's a large gap you physically can't cross without a **Hardlight Bridge (Pedestrian)**. You'll need to craft that plus a Laser Emitter and a Battery (Makeshift), and bring ~8 Tech Scrap.
- Before the main reactor door matters, it must first be activated in an underwater cave below the reactor — that's a separate step from opening the door itself.
- You'll also want your Gatekey (Tier 6) for the door once you're actually there.

**Mist Reactor**
- Reached by continuing past Cloud (through thick alien vegetation blocking the direct tram line — you traverse it on foot).
- The bottom floor has a keypad next to a rounded glass door — that one only needs a Level 5 Keypad, not 6.
- Getting through the door isn't the finish line: there are two status screens, and you need to destroy 5 obstructions scattered around the reactor before it shows "clear." Only then can you go back to the Control Room and power it up.

So the short version: your Level 6 keypad matters for Gale's door and general blast doors, but Cloud is a fight you push through rather than unlock, and Mist needs a Level 5 keypad plus clearing 5 obstructions before it'll actually power on. content.title: Abiotic Factor The Reactors Walkthrough | TechRaptor
content.text:
After jumping through Spillway C in the Hydroplant, you'll fall a short distance into The Reactors sector in Abiotic Factor. Don't worry about fall damage; you're safe. You'll land in water, so make sure to swim to the surface.

Our Abiotic Factor The Reactors Walkthrough will show you how to power up all four reactors and gain access to the WG-Intrados facility. After jumping through Spillway C in the Hydroplant, you'll fall a short distance into The Reactors sector in Abiotic Factor. Don't worry about fall damage; you're safe. You'll land in water, so make sure to swim to the surface. As soon as you land, turn to your right. You'll see pink webbing covering up a tunnel. If you destroy this webbing, you'll find sewers with a few zombies in them. More importantly, you can find multiple special crates including an Ornate Crate, a GATE Security Crate, a Cacophonus Crate, and two instances of the new Runic Crate. You can come back here later to open them up if you'd like. Swim to the left of where you dropped and you'll see giant lily pads of a sort making a path along the water.

There are two status screens in the reactor room. If you've destroyed all 5 obstructions, it will show as clear. You can then make your way back to the Control Room and power up the Mist Reactor. Now it's time to make our way to the Gale Reactor! Make your way back to your base; you'll have to craft a few items. There's a large gap to cross to reach the Gale Reactor, so you're going to want to craft a Hardlight Bridge (Pedestrian), a Laser Emitter, and a Battery (Makeshift). You'll also want to bring 8 or so Tech Scrap with you, along with all of your other usual equipment. You may want to try to cross the gap with wood bridges, but I assure you — using a Hardlight Bridge is much, much easier. You will also need the Gatekey (Tier 6). With the aquisition of the Heart of Corruption from killing the Corrupted Robot, you now have access to all of the components you'll need to make the next tier of Keypad.

The Gale Reactor is effectively a battleground between the Gatekeepers and the Order. Both of them are hostile to you, but they're also hostile to each other. I strongly recommend taking out the Gatekeepers on the left first; they're much tougher, and having them be distracted by the Order will make them easier to kill from the high ground. When they're dead, shift your attention to the Order soldiers on the right. When the lobby area is clear, it's time to go deeper into the facility. Like the lobby, it appears that the facility is split in half with the Order controlling one half and the Gatekeepers controlling the other half. There are two large open blast doors on either side of the bridge. The red door is Gatekeeper territory and the blue door is Order territory. As before, we'll tackle the Gatekeepers first; go through the red door. You will almost certainly encountered a Jotun to the left as you enter.

Go upstairs and you'll have to face multiple Neophytes. Kill them, then move past the blue eyes graffiti and the machinery on the upper level until you find a door that says "Gale Reactor." Go through this room and you'll encounter a Mystagogue. A second Mystagogue is nearby, so you may have to kill two of them. In this same room, you'll see glass double doors with a Gatekeeper Chieftan behind it. Kill the Gatekeeper Chieftan. Go down and to the left, following the signs to the Gale Reactor. When you actually get into the Gale Reactor, you'll see a strange console: Unlike previous reactors, you don't need to supply any Transuranic Superalloy. Instead, you need to push each of the three buttons in sequence to spawn waves of enemies to fight. You're going to face the toughest stuff the Gatekeepers can throw at you, so make sure you have plenty of ammo before starting.

content.title: How to activate Gale Reactor in Abiotic Factor - gamever
content.text:
Much of the Gale Reactor is underwater, which means you’ll need diving gear to explore certain sections. If you didn’t bring any, you’ll have to backtrack and find some before progressing. While swimming, keep an eye out for strange creatures lurking in the depths. Something is moving down there, and it’s not friendly. There are also submerged tunnels that may lead to hidden rooms or shortcuts, so it’s worth taking the time to explore. One of the most important things to find is a power cell, which is necessary for restoring energy to the facility. The reactor itself is locked behind multiple security measures, so you’ll need to disable them one by one. The first step is unlocking the doors leading to the control room. Some of these require keypads, and if you don’t already have the necessary codes, you might need to search the area for notes or terminals that provide hints.

The Gale Reactor is one of the most dangerous and complex areas in Abiotic Factor. Built over an underground lake, this facility is a warzone, with Gatekeepers and Order soldiers locked in constant battle. On top of that, the area is in ruins, with collapsed floors, missing walkways, and entire sections completely flooded. Getting to the Gale Reactor is tricky. The tram system that used to connect it to other locations is broken, meaning you’ll have to find an alternative way in. The easiest method is using a Jetpack or a Gravity Cube to launch yourself to the entrance, but if you don’t have those, you’ll need to get creative. Some players have built makeshift bridges using deployable objects like shelves, while others have used the Hard Light Bridge. This requires digital gold, arcane scrap, and flickering eyes from Mystagogues, so if you don’t have the materials yet, you might need to go scavenging first.

I need to correct something — the "underwater cave below the reactor" detail comes from a general wiki blurb, but it isn't specific about location, and the more detailed walkthrough I found doesn't describe that step at all for the current version of the game. I don't want to send you looking for a cave that may not be how it actually works anymore.

Here's what the detailed walkthrough actually describes for getting into and activating Gale, and it lines up with what you're set up for:

1. **Reaching the entrance:** Gale's tram is broken, so you cross a large gap using gear/deployables — this is exactly what your Hardlight Bridges are for. Bring your Gatekey (Tier 6) too.
2. **Clearing the lobby:** Once across, you land in a lobby split between Gatekeepers (left) and Order (right), fighting each other. Kill the Gatekeepers first — they're tougher — while they're distracted by the Order.
3. **Two wings, two doors:** Past the lobby, there's a red door (Gatekeeper side) and a blue door (Order side), split by a bridge. Clear the red side first — expect a Jotun, then upstairs Neophytes, then a couple Mystagogues, then a Gatekeeper Chieftain behind glass doors.
4. **Finding Gale Reactor itself:** Following the signs down and to the left after clearing that gets you to the actual "Gale Reactor" door.
5. **Activating it:** Inside, there's a console with three buttons. Unlike the other reactors, you don't feed it Transuranic Superalloy — pressing each button in sequence spawns waves of Gatekeeper enemies, and you have to fight through all three waves to activate it. Come in stocked on ammo.

Given what you've told me you have (bridges, weapons, teleporter anchor point already near the gate camp), you're set up well for this — the fight is the real gate here, not a specific cave or hidden switch.

content.title: Maestro Set obtaining :: Abiotic Factor 💡 Scientific Suggestions
content.text:
Originally posted by Blackforge:It's not a mandatory armor to get though. Technically any content that isn't blocking the "golden path" (the road to progress the game) isn't mandatory. This doesn't mean it is not worth showing the player all the possible ways to interact with the content. While balancing is quite subjective (how many shards/organs and how often they drop), the exposition of the content is quite an objective task for the game developer. For instance, the Hexed armor set deals much better with familiarizing us with obtaining it. Hexwood is introduced as a relevant crafting resource (small sign, mannequins, bucket), with few recipes that require only things found earlier(mostly in labs or office sectors). Later, we can pick up Kevlar Scraps in the security sector at a very early stage. This alone leads to discovering 3 of 4 items that make the Hexed Set.

Originally posted by Favouritism ❤ ain't my thing:During my playthrough, I realized there is an armor set that you can skip without realizing it. The offender is of course Maestro Set, due to its lack of exposition. As probably everyone knows, we get the Idea of creating a new item by obtaining all the components that build it. Usually, this works fine unless an item requires something with a low drop rate (In this instance it is the Organ). On average, you need to kill 10 symphonists to learn that an armor set can be built from their loot. This wouldn't be the problem itself, but if we take into account that: Symphonists are quite durable and powerful enemies(especially at the stage we can encounter them) We don't have guaranteed encounters with them(we can't control the occurrence of the fog in the facility and Flathills can generate without any guaranteed encounter) An alternative way to obtain the organ is to combine partial organs obtained from fishing.

Originally posted by Blackforge:It's not a mandatory armor to get though. Technically any content that isn't blocking the "golden path" (the road to progress the game) isn't mandatory. This doesn't mean it is not worth showing the player all the possible ways to interact with the content. Later, we can pick up Kevlar Scraps in the security sector at a very early stage. This alone leads to discovering 3 of 4 items that make the Hexed Set.

Change the crafting recipe of both Maestro Vambraces and Graves to require the "Partial Organs" (2-3 per piece). Reduce the amount of "Partial Organs" needed to craft an "Organ" from 5 to 4 ... A bit of a tangent, but it would go faster if, Porcelain Keys actually dropped from Symphonists! I've killed like 33 of them (I know, I kept all the heads) and found no keys! And a few keys would help give us more materials for making the Maestro Set. And that's with dang near guaranteed encounters. I've got a base in the HQ office, and more often than not, there is a Symphonist right there, luring around near the elevator, with one or two others in Flathill. After farming the area I'd go off and do other things while waiting for respawns. I've got so many practically useless heads. Why can't we turn them into something more useful? ... I didn't get my first porcelain key until deep into the Hydroplant. It's crazy. ... It's not a mandatory armor to get though.

While there are many viable ways to familiarize the players with their possibilities (for example adding a crafting recipe that requires only porcelain shards and items we found prior in the facility), I think that rebalancing the drops of the Symphonists is the most reasonable, especially considering the scope of the update that will introduce the Reactor. ... Any change to make the Maestro set more feasible to get without refreshing flathill countless times or fishing for ages is a great change in my book. I farmed for it right after finishing Flathill on my last save, just to see how it performs at the stage of the game you unlock it at and the whole process took a ridiculous amount of time. Which is even more of a shame with how fun of an armor set it is to use. ... Even in solo, where you only want one, the armor set is too hard to get in a reasonable amount of time before it gets 'out dated' or overshadowed by other things.

Confirmed — you're right, my mistake. The **Hexwood Shield** is its own separate item (Off-Hand Armament slot, not part of the Hex Armor Set), and it's not what I described as the "Accursed Hood." My apologies for the confusion there.

The actual recipe is: **4 Hexwood, 2 Kevlar Scrap, 2 Snag Vine Seed, 4 Box of Screws** (crafted at a Crafting Bench).

So you're a bit short on my earlier read — it's not just 2 Kevlar Scrap and a Snag Vine Seed, it's 2 Kevlar Scrap and **2** Snag Vine Seeds, plus 4 Hexwood and 4 Box of Screws (which you said you can make). If you've already got the Hexwood stockpiled from the armor set farming, you're most of the way there.

A couple practical notes on the shield itself:
- It's a **light** shield class, so it only reflects/blocks "light" class projectiles — not everything.
- It regenerates 2 durability every 60 seconds on its own, same as the rest of the Hex gear, so it fits your no-repair, no-ammo playstyle.
- It has a known bug where if it breaks, it can get stuck acting "broken" even after regenerating durability — unequip and re-equip it to fix that if it happens.

And your plan of pairing it with the Mushroom Helmet instead of Accursed Hood makes sense — you get spore/disease protection there and can still run the rest of the Hex set (Breastplate, Bindings, Shinplates) for the bleed-healing bonuses, with the shield handling your block/damage-reflection role instead of a helmet.

content.title: Abiotic Factor Resources Guide | Where to Find Crafting Materials
content.text:
This guide will tell you how to get the Abiotic Factor crafting materials you'll need to craft useful items and build defenses for your base.

You can get Hexwood by killing the sapient trees in the Canaan Portal World. You can also get Hexwood by scrapping certain items such as the Woodsman's Axe which can be dropped by the Canaanites who wield them. You can find a Hose in Bio Lab D on the second floor of the Office Sector. You can also find Hoses in various other industrial settings such as Manufacturing West, especially in the crates marked with orange and black stripes. A Hose is one of the items that you'll get from scrapping a Fire Extinguisher. Hoses are required to complete some of the objectives in Manufacturing West. You'll also need these for farming. You can get a Human Arm (Military) by killing an Order soldier and chopping up their corpse with a Knife or any other suitable Sharp Melee weapon such as the Makeshift Spear. You are not guaranteed to get one as a drop. You can get a Human Brain by scrapping a Human Skull at a Repair & Salvage Station.

There are tons of crafting materials to collect in Abiotic Factor, but not all of them are easy to find. Keep reading for more details on the important items you need to survive! Here are all of the Abiotic Factor crafting materials we've found so far. You can get an Anomaly by equipping a Test Tube on your hotbar and interacting with the glowing orbs of light that appear in the GATE Facility at night. Anomalies are used in a handful of crafting recipes and they can be traded to The Blacksmith for Rebar. You can get Anteverse Gel by traveling to The Mycofields and collecting it from the purple rocks. Anteverse Gel is used to make Antithermite, a critical item required to unlock Rise and the Security Sector. A small amount of Anteverse Gel can also be found in Village Den da'ko Yeer. You can find Anteverse Gem throughout the Adjustment Wing in the Cascade Laboratories Sector; it's typically located within special white boxes that contain it.

That's the end of our Abiotic Factor Crafting Materials Guide. Make sure to check out our other guides below! ... One of my earliest memories is playing Super Mario Bros. on the Nintendo Entertainment System. I've had a controller in my hand since I was 4…

The Defunct Shield Generator is an incredibly rare item. There's a good chance that you'll find one in a Runic Crate. Outside of that, you'll have to get lucky and get this rare drop from a Gatekeeper. You can get a Desk Leg by destroying most pieces of furniture such as coffee tables, sofas, and desks. Desk Legs aren't used for much beyond the early-game weapons, so don't hold onto too many of them in your storage. You can find a Desk Phone sitting on top of a desk in most office areas throughout the GATE Facility. You can only get Digital Ore by salvaging Royal Coins and Royal Crowns from Space Queen, a Portal World contained in an arcade machine in the Cascade Laboratories. You can get a Diode by trading Axle Grease to the Blacksmith in Manufacturing West. Diodes are used to craft some of the more advanced tech needed for The Labs. You can find Duct Tape lying around in industrial-themed areas and storage rooms.

This guide will tell you how Abiotic Factor crafting works and how to unlock new crafting recipes. We also have a long list of crafting recipes! Crafting is a big part of Abiotic Factor — you'll need to make a lot of stuff to properly defend your base and equip yourself for exploring the map. Read on to learn what you need to know about crafting! You'll mainly craft items in Abiotic Factor by using a powered Crafting Bench. You can craft a handful of items by hand in your inventory (including the Crafting Bench), but the vast majority of crafted items will require a powered Crafting Bench. Note that you can also "un-Craft" items in a way by scrapping them using the Repair & Salvage Station. This will destroy the item and give you a small portion of the resources used to make the item. In some cases, scrapping is the only way to get access to some resources in the early game.

## Usage

The Hexwood Shield is a light [shield blocking class](https://abioticfactor.wiki.gg/wiki/Off-Hand_Armaments#Shield_Blocking_Classes "Off-Hand Armaments") armament and can only reflect projectiles in the "light" class. Hexwood Shield cannot be repaired, but regenerates 2 points of durability every 60 seconds.

## Sources

Hexwood Shield can only be obtained through Crafting.

## Notes

- Although the Hexwood Shield has a listed durability of 30, the game does not consider it fully repaired until its durability is *above* 30. As a result, its durability will continue to increase until it reaches either 31 or 32.
- The Hexwood Shield is capable of creating short-lived, [Snag Vine](https://abioticfactor.wiki.gg/wiki/Snag_Vine "Snag Vine")-like growths around attackers in response to a blocked hit. However, due to a bug in the vines' spawning position, this is rare and can only happen in specific locations.
- If the Hexwood Shield breaks, it may continue to behave as a broken shield after regenerating durability, failing to block any additional incoming attacks. This can be fixed by unequipping and re-equipping the shield.

Confirmed — you're right, my mistake. The **Hexwood Shield** is its own separate item (Off-Hand Armament slot, not part of the Hex Armor Set), and it's not what I described as the "Accursed Hood." My apologies for the confusion there.

The actual recipe is: **4 Hexwood, 2 Kevlar Scrap, 2 Snag Vine Seed, 4 Box of Screws** (crafted at a Crafting Bench).

So you're a bit short on my earlier read — it's not just 2 Kevlar Scrap and a Snag Vine Seed, it's 2 Kevlar Scrap and **2** Snag Vine Seeds, plus 4 Hexwood and 4 Box of Screws (which you said you can make). If you've already got the Hexwood stockpiled from the armor set farming, you're most of the way there.

A couple practical notes on the shield itself:
- It's a **light** shield class, so it only reflects/blocks "light" class projectiles — not everything.
- It regenerates 2 durability every 60 seconds on its own, same as the rest of the Hex gear, so it fits your no-repair, no-ammo playstyle.
- It has a known bug where if it breaks, it can get stuck acting "broken" even after regenerating durability — unequip and re-equip it to fix that if it happens.

This study was carried out at the El Zafire Biological Station in the Colombian Amazon at 4°0’21”S and 69°53’55” W ([Fig fig1]). We used seedlings from the trees *Caraipa* sp. (Clusiaceae) and *Tachigali* sp. (Fabaceae), for which we located 10 seedling banks (i.e., 10 parent trees) and *Dicranostyles* sp. (Convolvulaceae) for which eight seedling banks were found.

To apply the different treatments we planted groups of 10 seedlings per treatment in the forest and in the shade house.

## Forest experiment

Under each parent tree we randomly allocated 10 seedlings to each of the following treatments:

Added fertilizer (hypothesis 1)
Excluded from the parental roots (hypothesis 2)
Planted on soil collected far from the parent tree (hypotheses 3 and 4).
Control: unearthed and replanted seedlings to account for the manipulation of all seedlings.


## Shade house experiment

Not exclusively — the Night Realm is one source, but not the only one. Snag Vine Seeds turn up in a few places:

- **The Mines** — near the door leading to the pool of Antejuice.
- **Containment Block** — there's a Snag Vine growing from a drain in a detainment cell near the tram station. Some players note that letting the big guy (the Reaper/Dirac encounter) break your legs and grabbing them from the holding room is an easy way to snag this one.
- **The Night Realm** (your "weird night place") — you can find up to **four** here, scattered somewhat randomly near where trees/plants grow.
- **Divarcation in Fragments** — one more can be found there.
- **Scrapping an existing Snag Vine** at a Repair & Salvage Station also gives a seed, if you find one already planted/grown somewhere.

Since you're deep in the Reactors now, the Night Realm and Containment/Mines are all backtrack territory — but worth noting there's no renewable farm for these: growing one out in a Garden Plot won't give you extra seeds back, only the placeable vine itself. So whatever seeds you gather are it until you go find more in the world. For just 2 seeds, checking the Containment cell near the tram (if you remember passing through there) is probably your fastest bet since it doesn't require a special portal trip.
